title: New Outlook will stop users changing Default and Anonymous folder permissions when your organisation restricts them
summary: Roadmap item RM579185 (In development, GA targeted January 2027, worldwide, new Outlook for Windows and web) makes folder sharing in Outlook respect organisational restrictions on Default and Anonymous permissions: with the restriction enabled, users cannot change either setting. Permissions granted directly to named users are unaffected.
why: Default and Anonymous folder permissions are a classic quiet over-share (and an internal recon gift: a Reviewer grant on Default exposes a mailbox folder to every user in the tenant). Client-side enforcement helps only if the org-level restriction is actually set, and the roadmap entry does not name the setting — so plan on auditing existing grants, which the change does not remove.
todo: Audit existing grants now: `Get-EXOMailboxFolderPermission` per folder, filtering on User Default and Anonymous with an access right other than None/AvailabilityOnly.
Watch for the Exchange Online setting that backs the restriction before January 2027 and decide whether to enable it.
Remember calendar sharing with free/busy for Default is normal; target content-level rights on mail and calendar folders.
effective_note: GA targeted January 2027 (RM579185); controlling setting not named in the roadmap entry.
